basics.name: Jonathan K. Sakkos
basics.label: Staff Engineer, Spatial Genomics R&D
basics.throughline: I turn biology into products by building the instruments, software, and processes in between.
basics.accent: the instruments, software, and processes in between
intro: I'm a Staff Engineer in Spatial Genomics R&D at Takara Bio USA, where I lead engineering for spatial transcriptomics products from early research through manufacturing launch. The work doesn't fit neatly into one discipline, and that's the point: automated instruments, computer-vision pipelines, production fixtures, and the validation that lets operations own them.

I got here the long way: designing wear parts for a steel foundry, a Ph.D. in mechanical engineering spent putting bacteria inside silica gels, and a postdoc engineering cyanobacteria. Most engineers own one layer. I like owning the whole chain, so nothing gets lost in the hand-offs.
story: My first engineering job was at Columbia Steel Casting in Portland, designing replacement wear parts for industrial scrap shredders. It taught me to follow a design all the way through: from the engineering request to the pattern shop, the foundry floor, and the customer.

In graduate school at the University of Minnesota I traded steel for living materials: porous silica gels that encapsulate bacteria so they can clean pollutants from water and run chemistry. A postdoc at Michigan State took me deeper into the biology, engineering cyanobacteria and modeling how microbial communities grow together, with the microscopy and image analysis to measure it.

In 2022 I joined Curio Bioscience to help turn its spatial transcriptomics workflows into manufacturing. Curio became part of Takara Bio in 2025, where I now lead engineering for spatial genomics products: the instruments, the image analysis, the fixtures, and the validation that hands them to operations.
basics.offTheClock: Off the clock I build open-source tools like Engram, take photos, cook, run a self-hosted homelab, and commute by bike and Caltrain, which is how I ended up tracking every train on the line.

work.summary: R&D engineering lead for spatial genomics product development, taking Seeker® and Trekker® products from research through manufacturing. I own the engineering across instruments, image analysis, fixtures, and design transfer.
highlights: Designed and validated a next-generation automated indexing instrument with multi-fold capacity per station, then qualified it and transferred it to operations.
Replaced a legacy MATLAB image-analysis pipeline with a validated Python and computer-vision system that runs several times faster, now in production with automated reporting.
Engineered the tissue-alignment fixture behind the Trekker® FX FFPE kit, winner of The Scientist's 2026 Top Innovations award.
Built automated QC and imaging-setup tools that let manufacturing run without R&D intervention.
Lead the cross-functional core team developing new custom tile formats for research customers, working with Operations, QA, and vendors through stage gates.

work.summary: Turned research-scale spatial transcriptomics workflows into manufacturable processes for the Seeker® and Trekker® product lines. Curio was acquired by Takara Bio in January 2025.
highlights: Started the automation and indexing scale-up program that became the next-generation production platform.
Built automated QC and process-automation tools that reduced manual intervention.

work.summary: Joined the spatial transcriptomics startup to turn its research workflows into manufacturing.
highlights: Developed and scaled manufacturing processes through the commercial launch of Seeker® and Trekker®.
Designed custom fixtures with CAD and 3D printing to speed up R&D cycles.
Established QC checks and standard operating procedures for new processes.

work.summary: Synthetic biology of cyanobacteria and microbial communities in the Ducat Lab, combining lab experiments with computational modeling and image analysis.
highlights: Developed genetic tools for engineering photosynthetic microbes, including an orthogonal protein-degradation system and quorum-sensing circuits.
Combined experiments with agent-based modeling (NUFEB) and neural-network surrogate models to study light-driven microbial communities.
Applied automated microscopy and deep learning to quantify cellular structures, with collaborators at Oak Ridge National Laboratory.
Led a small research team and mentored graduate and undergraduate researchers; 8 papers from this period.

work.summary: Engineered living materials: porous silica gels that encapsulate bacteria for water remediation and biocatalysis.
highlights: Designed, synthesized, and characterized porous sol-gel silica materials for encapsulating bacteria.
Authored 7 peer-reviewed papers and filed 3 patent applications.

work.summary: Designed replacement wear parts for heavy scrap shredders, from engineering request through foundry production and sales. Started as an intern in 2007.
highlights: Modeled parts and assemblies in SolidWorks and produced drawings in AutoCAD.
Redesigned parts for longer service life, working with the pattern shop and foundry to avoid production issues.

projects.name: Engram
projects.pitch: Open-source disc ripping and media organization with a live web dashboard. It identifies TV episodes by audio fingerprint and asks a human when a disc is ambiguous, instead of guessing.

projects.name: Caltrain Performance Tracker
projects.pitch: Logs the position of every Caltrain once a minute and turns it into on-time performance, delay patterns, and space-time diagrams of incidents.

projects.name: PhotoSift
projects.pitch: A local-first photo pipeline: import a card, let on-device models group and annotate the shots, then cull with one keystroke per photo. Decisions land in XMP sidecars for Lightroom.

projects.name: lr-autotag
projects.pitch: AI keyword tagging for Lightroom Classic catalogs, using CLIP to match photos against a keyword hierarchy.

projects.name: MKV Episode Matcher
projects.pitch: Identifies and renames ripped TV episodes using speech recognition and fuzzy matching. The predecessor to Engram.

projects.name: AirIQ
projects.pitch: An indoor air-quality meter that measures CO₂, particulates, VOCs, temperature, humidity, and pressure, with an LED that shows the PM2.5 AQI by color.

projects.name: Cat Wheel Speedometer
projects.pitch: A speedometer for a cat's exercise wheel: a reed switch and magnets measure speed and distance, logged to Home Assistant.

projects.name: NUFEB contributions and nufeb_tools
projects.pitch: Added cyanobacteria and quorum-sensing models to the open-source NUFEB biofilm simulator, plus Python tools for setting up and analyzing simulations.

projects.name: microtools
projects.pitch: Python tools for analyzing microscopy images.
